post.title: Nvidia Fell to a 7-Month Low While AMD Recovered 📉
post.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) fell 5.5% on Tuesday, Nov 10, to $168.89, its lowest close since March 30. It's down 9.5% in two sessions and 29.4% from its Oct 6 close.

Tuesday's big movers:
📈 Charter Communications (CHTR) +10.6%
📈 Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) +8.3%, after beating earnings (EPS $0.99 vs −$0.59 expected)
📈 Rocket Lab (RKLB) +6.5%, despite missing earnings estimates (EPS −$0.08 vs −$0.06 expected)
📉 Nvidia (NVDA) −5.5%
📉 Barrick Mining (B) −6.1%
📉 Moderna (MRNA) −6.8%

Since last Wednesday's close (Nov 4), before Thursday's chip crash:
📈 AMD +5.4%
📉 Micron (MU) −8.8%
📉 Nvidia (NVDA) −15.6%

S&P 500 (SPY): −0.4% · Nasdaq 100 (QQQ): −0.7% · Dow (DIA): −0.3%

AMD or Nvidia: which would you pick? Tell me in the comments.
Subscribe for the market's biggest moves every trading day.

Moves use official closing prices. Data: Robinhood. Narrated with an AI voice. Not financial advice.

scenes.say: Nvidia fell five and a half percent on Tuesday... to its lowest close in more than seven months.

Charter jumped almost eleven percent. Take-Two rose eight after beating earnings, and Rocket Lab six and a half, even though it missed estimates. But Nvidia fell five and a half percent, gold miner Barrick six, and Moderna almost seven.

scenes.say: Here's Nvidia since late September. It peaked on October sixth... and it's been sliding since. Monday and Tuesday alone took off nine and a half percent, leaving it twenty nine percent below that peak.
Now compare AMD. Since last Wednesday's close, before the chip crash, AMD is up five percent. Micron is down almost nine... and Nvidia is down almost sixteen.
